subject: Clarification: SLO measurement, monitoring access, and exception for scheduled batch windows
messages:
From: Dan Cho <dan.cho@acmehealth.com>
To: evelyn.hart@redwood.com
Cc: procurement@acmehealth.com, selene.carter@acmehealth.com
Date: Mon, 3 May 2027 15:12:00 -0700
Subject: Measurement & access questions for SLOs during scheduled batch windows

Evelyn,

Thanks for taking our procurement questionnaire — a couple of follow-ups from the ops team as we prepare contract language. Our workload has a daily high-throughput batch window (00:00–03:00 UTC) that frequently pushes per-request latency beyond normal interactive SLAs. We need clarity on two things before we sign:

1) Measurement: How will Redwood compute uptime/latency SLIs during predictable high-throughput windows? Specifically, do you support: exclusion windows, maintenance windows, or an explicit exception addendum? What percentile(s) do you use (p95/p99) and where is latency measured (edge vs. service egress)?

2) Monitoring & access: We need read-only access to the dashboard that shows raw sampling and the time-series used to calculate SLOs. Can we get SSO-backed Grafana access or a data export? Also: how are alerts generated (noise filtering, grouping) and can they integrate with our PagerDuty?

Finally, for audit/compliance we need an assurance that any approved exception is recorded in an auditable way (who approved, duration, reason). Can you provide sample contract language for an exception so our legal team can review?

I attached our completed procurement questionnaire PDF (procurement_questionnaire_filled.pdf) with the sections referenced. Please loop in the appropriate product/ops folks.

Best,
Dan
Dan Cho
Director, Platform Engineering
Acme Health

Subject: Re: Measurement & access questions for SLOs during scheduled batch windows

Hi Dan / Selene / Acme procurement team,

Thanks — great questions. I pulled the relevant details together below and attached our SLO metrics playbook and a draft exception addendum for your review. I'll summarize first, then include the technical specifics.

Summary (short answers)
- Measurement: Redwood computes latency SLIs at the service egress (post-routing, pre-response). We report p95 and p99 per-route and global p99 for interactive endpoints. Uptime is calculated as the percentage of successful, non-error responses within the configured latency threshold over the evaluation window.
- Exclusions/Exceptions: We support a documented "SLO Exception Addendum" for predictable windows (e.g., nightly batch runs). Exceptions are contractually recorded, time-boxed, and subject to compensating credits in certain plans.
- Monitoring & Access: Read-only dashboards (Grafana) are available via SSO for customers with Dedicated or Private deployments; hosted customers can request a dashboard share or a scheduled metrics export. Alerts integrate with PagerDuty and support threshold and trend-based rules plus noise suppression logic. Audit logs record changes to SLOs and exception approvals.

Technical details
- Latency SLI: measured at egress, bucketed by route/endpoint. Default thresholds: interactive endpoints 300ms (p95), 500ms (p99). Batch/ingest endpoints are measured separately with configurable thresholds.
- Uptime SLI: successful_response_count / total_request_count within the window. Health checks and synthetic probes are included in the dashboard but excluded from the customer-facing SLO metric by default.
- Sampling: we use deterministic sampling for low-volume routes and adaptive sampling for high-throughput customers to keep storage bounded while preserving p99 fidelity. Typical sampling is 100% for interactive traffic and 10–25% for bulk flows; we retain raw samples for 30 days by default, aggregated metrics for 13 months.
- Alerts: alerting rules can be configured by account; severe SLO breaches trigger a PagerDuty incident (configurable escalation), while minor trend alerts are sent as quieter notifications.
- Exceptions: the process is: (1) customer requests window, (2) Redwood product/ops assesses impact, (3) exception is recorded as an SLO Exception Addendum (start/end + rationale), (4) exception is versioned in audit logs and linked to the account.

Next steps / ask of you
- Please confirm the exact UTC window you want excluded (e.g., 00:00–03:00 UTC nightly) and whether you want the exception to be recurring or a one-off.
- If you want the dashboard share, tell us which email(s) to grant SSO access to. For hosted customers we can provide scheduled CSV exports if SSO is not available.

Attachments: redwood-slo-metrics-playbook.pdf, slo-exception-addendum-draft.docx

Happy to hop on a 30-minute call if you prefer to walk through the clause.

Thanks,
Evelyn Hart
Senior Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference

Evelyn — thanks for the detailed breakdown, that helps. Two quick follow-ups:

1) Exclusions: Will the SLO calculation exclude the scheduled window entirely (i.e., remove data points in the 00:00–03:00 UTC window from the numerator/denominator), or will Redwood apply a compensating policy (e.g., count but apply a different threshold)? We need the exact behavior defined so our SLAs with downstream teams are clear.

2) Auditability: For regulatory reasons we require an immutable record of who approved an exception and when. Is the audit log exportable, and what retention does it have?

If you can paste sample contract wording for the clause, that would make legal review faster. We're aiming for a decision this week.

Thanks,
Dan

Subject: Re: Measurement & access questions for SLOs during scheduled batch windows — sample clause and audit details

Hi Dan — looping in product and legal-friendly phrasing. Below is a concise sample clause we've used with other customers; happy to tighten language to match Acme's contract templates.

Sample clause (proposed)
"SLO Exception Addendum: Redwood Inference and Customer may mutually agree to one or more time-boxed SLO exceptions (\"Exception\") for predictable, scheduled workload windows. An Exception must be documented in writing and include: start and end timestamps, the scope of affected routes/endpoints, and the approving Redwood representative. During an Exception the affected data points will be excluded from the computation of Customer-facing SLOs for the agreed period. Exceptions will be recorded in Redwood's audit logs and retained for a minimum of 24 months. Where applicable, commercial remedies (SLO credits) will be applied as specified in the applicable Order Form."

Audit & exports
- Audit logs: All SLO and Exception records include a timestamp, initiating account, and approver identity (internal RFC/ID). Logs are exportable as CSV via the Customer Console for Dedicated/Private customers; for hosted customers exports are provided on request as part of procurement deliveries. Retention: 24 months by default.
- Dashboard access: We can enable read-only Grafana access via SSO for the named user emails, or provide scheduled CSV exports covering the raw samples used in SLO calc if SSO is not permitted by Acme.

Attachments: I attached an editable addendum draft (slo-exception-addendum-draft.docx) and the internal playbook (redwood-slo-metrics-playbook.pdf). We can also provision a 30-day trial of expanded dashboard access so your team can validate measurements against your internal metrics.

Please confirm: (a) recurring vs one-off, (b) exact UTC window, (c) emails for SSO access (if desired). Once confirmed we'll generate a formal addendum and record the exception in the account with audit metadata.

Thanks,
Rishi Malhotra
Director, Product — Observability, Redwood Inference
Attachment: slo-exception-addendum-draft.docx (docx), redwood-slo-metrics-playbook.pdf (pdf)
